gap: No result ChatGPT got states that FiiO's own DM13 page says the standard DM13 cannot send Bluetooth at all (only the BT version can), and that even the BT version 'may not be supported' by some car Bluetooth systems, so a buyer needs the BT SKU plus a 3.5 mm line-out-to-AUX fallback.
standout_why: I opened itechguides.com (2026-10-11) and ensightauto.com (2026-02-04). itechguides covers Bluetooth limits only through generic Amazon listings: MEGATEK is 'Not compatible with Bluetooth car stereos' and Sunoony 'cannot transmit audio via Bluetooth'. It also warns that 'a generic USB CD drive is not automatically compatible'. Ensight says only that a USB port 'that supports audio playback' is the key requirement and that most 2016+ touchscreen cars 'qualify'. Neither page names the FiiO DM13, the split between its standard and BT versions, FiiO's own car-Bluetooth caveat, or its FAT32-only USB ripping. Both pages have part of the general Bluetooth caveat, but none has these maker-stated limits for a product on our page. I could not read the navtv.com PDF (certificate error), the manuals.plus pages (403) or the m.media-amazon.com AIE PDF (a scanned image, no text), so I can't rule out that one of them has vehicle-level fit data.
decides: This confirms the page should list the FiiO DM13 *BT* SKU, not the cheaper standard DM13. It should also say plainly that the DM13's Bluetooth to a car stereo is not guaranteed by FiiO, so the 3.5 mm line-out to AUX is the dependable route and cars with neither AUX nor working Bluetooth audio should go to an in-dash CD receiver. For the in-dash picks, Pioneer's manual lists only USB mass-storage (MSC) and MTP devices on FAT12/16/32. That makes the deck's own CD slot, not an add-on USB CD drive, the documented way to play discs.

findings.label: Bluetooth transmit depends on version
findings.value: Only the BT version transmits; FiiO: "Standard version cannot transmit Bluetooth"
findings.note: Maker's product page. Dealectric's slug is fiio-dm13-bt, so the page should name the BT variant.

findings.label: Car Bluetooth compatibility caveat
findings.value: FiiO: "Some car Bluetooth systems and specific headphone/speaker models may not be supported"
findings.note: Exclusion stated by the maker. FiiO names no specific car makes or head units.

findings.label: Bluetooth transmit codecs
findings.value: aptX, aptX Low Latency, aptX HD, SBC; some receivers may fall back to SBC only
findings.note: FiiO says some headphones or speakers support only SBC because of chipset and protocol limits.

findings.label: Wired outputs usable in a car
findings.value: Single-ended and balanced line outs (for active speakers or amps), plus optical and coaxial digital out; 3.5 mm and 4.4 mm headphone outs
findings.note: A car AUX input takes the single-ended 3.5 mm line out. A 3.5 mm coaxial adapter is in the box.

findings.label: USB-C role
findings.value: Power and data. D.MODE runs the unit from USB power without drawing the battery. Rips CDs to WAV on a USB drive, FAT32 only (FiiO recommends a Type-C flash drive of 32 GB or less). FiiO does not say it works as a USB audio or CD source for a car head unit.
findings.note: So the DM13 cannot stand in for a 'plug into the car's USB port' CD drive. Its car routes are Bluetooth or line-out to AUX.

findings.label: Disc read limits
findings.value: FiiO says the unit "cannot perfectly read all CD discs" and that frame skipping on some CD-R/CD-RW discs is normal; 10 h battery (FiiO lab data, 3,750 mAh 3.8 V)
findings.note: This is the maker's own exclusion for burned discs. The page does not list MP3-CD support.

findings.label: Manual covers which models
findings.value: One operation manual covers the DEH-S5200BT, DEH-S4220BT and DEH-S4200BT
findings.source_title: Pioneer DEH-S5200BT / DEH-S4220BT / DEH-S4200BT Operation Manual (ManualsLib copy)
findings.note: Cover page, plus page 42 'also suitable for'. This is a third-party copy of Pioneer's document; usa.pioneer returned HTTP 429 three times.

findings.label: USB device compatibility
findings.value: File system FAT12/FAT16/FAT32; USB protocol MSC (mass storage) or MTP; "Pioneer cannot guarantee compatibility with all USB mass storage devices"
findings.source_title: Pioneer DEH-S5200BT / DEH-S4220BT / DEH-S4200BT Operation Manual (ManualsLib copy)
findings.note: From pages 36 and 40. No other USB source class (such as an external CD drive) is listed. I'm inferring, not quoting, that a USB CD drive is not a documented source.

findings.label: iPhone and app limits
findings.value: Some functions need the iPhone connected to Pioneer Smart Sync over USB; Pandora is "Not available when [USB MTP] is set to [ON]"
findings.source_title: Pioneer DEH-S5200BT / DEH-S4220BT / DEH-S4200BT Operation Manual (ManualsLib copy)
findings.note: Pages 10 and 15. The excerpt I could read had no list of supported iPhone models.

findings.label: Rival claim on which cars take a USB CD drive
findings.value: Ensight: needs a USB port 'that supports audio playback — not just charging'; 'Most vehicles 2016 and newer with touchscreen infotainment systems qualify'; you may have to unplug the CD drive to use CarPlay on a single-port car; no DVD or CD+G graphics
findings.source_title: How to Add a CD Player to a Car That Doesn't Have One – Ensight Automotive Solutions
findings.note: Seller marketing on a rival page ChatGPT got. Recorded to show what rivals already cover; it is not a maker fit chart.
